title: Stop-queue avalanche: staged soft-reclaim and per-tenant slow-start
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Follow-up ticket from the Feb 17 hosted API degradation where sustained tenant bursts triggered GPU pool depletion. This issue captures the proposed staged soft-reclaim algorithm, a per-tenant slow-start admission path, and associated telemetry and rollout plans to prevent queue avalanches caused by long-tail request storms and KV-cache pollution.
incident_summary: On 2026-02-17 04:30 UTC a combination of a prefetch coordinator regression and several large tenant bursts caused the GPU pool to enter an amplification loop: large numbers of queued requests with high sequence-length variance caused KV cache pollution and increased per-request processing time, which prevented autoscaler from priming capacity fast enough and triggered aggressive soft-throttles that cascaded into broad request failures and elevated latency for ~27 minutes.
timeline: 2026-02-17 04:28 UTC: First error spike observed in hosted-gpu-latency-prod (alerts page).
2026-02-17 04:30 UTC: On-call acknowledged; initial mitigation: raised soft throttle to 80% for non-critical lanes.
2026-02-17 04:34 UTC: Autoscaler attempted scale-up but observed high tail latencies and delayed slot provisioning.
2026-02-17 04:41 UTC: Manual emergency capacity priming to add two G4 pools completed; latency returned toward baseline by 04:55 UTC.
2026-02-17 05:15 UTC: Post-incident triage began; reproduction run in staging confirmed KV cache pollution pattern when heterogeneous sequence-length requests arrive in short window.
root_cause: Regression in prefetch coordinator (PR #4521) changed prefill ordering so that large, high-seq-length requests were preferentially prefetched into hot KV slots. When multiple tenants burst concurrently, this caused cache thrashing and resulted in higher per-token processing time. The autoscaler reacted to amplified latency signals but was rate-limited by cold-start latency for new GPU slots, creating a positive feedback loop and queue buildup.
immediate_mitigation: Reverted prefetch coordinator change (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/4521) — rolled to canary within 15 minutes.
Temporarily tightened tenant burst caps (control-plane config) to 50 requests/min for large-model lanes for 48h.
Enabled emergency fast-priming for autoscaler to allocate ephemeral warm instances for 10 minutes when tail latency > 1.2s.
Applied targeted eviction policy that deprioritized long-running prefetches from known noisy tenants.
long_term_action_items: Implement staged soft-reclaim: allow reclaim of up to X slots per pool per 30s window using 'interruptible' eviction to preserve hot KV segments (owner: Marcos Alvarez, due: 2026-03-24, estimate: 3).

Build per-tenant slow-start admission path that ramps token throughput over first N seconds to warm KV cache without triggering autoscaler oscillation (owner: Priya Menon, due: 2026-04-07, estimate: 5).
Introduce 'cache-affinity' scheduler improvement that groups similar sequence-length requests into packing windows to reduce KV cache churn (owner: Chen Wu, due: 2026-04-21, estimate: 8).
Autoscaler: add 'warm-slot' fast-priming path with lower cold-start penalty using pre-provisioned lightweight VMs for immediate short bursts (owner: Platform Infra, due: 2026-05-05, estimate: 8).
Add chaos tests for multi-tenant burst scenarios to prevent regressions (owner: SRE team, due: 2026-03-31, estimate: 3).
telemetry_changes: Add 'KV cache miss rate by tenant' panel to gpu-queue dashboard (panel: https://dashboard.redwood.ai/d/queues/gpu-kv?panelId=7).
Emit new metric: runtime.prefetch.interruptions_per_min by pool and tenant.
Instrument admission path for 'slow-start ramp percent' and track correlation with autoscaler decisions.
Create a synthetic multi-tenant burst alert that fires when queue growth > 200% and KV-cache-miss increases > 30% in 1 minute.
notes: Decision: prefer a soft-reclaim algorithm that preserves hot KV regions over blunt eviction; judged lower-risk to customer quality despite slightly longer recovery times.
Trade-off: the per-tenant slow-start will add marginal latency for first N tokens for some requests but reduces probability of broad degradation — PM aligned.
Review feedback: Security asked for a brief KMS impact statement; confirmed no key accesses are required by these changes.
Follow-up: schedule customer communications for impacted customers once long-term fixes are staged to canary (owner: CX lead).
